newsitem.title: FRANCE: French consumer sentiment edges higher in February.
newsitem.headline: French consumer sentiment edges higher in February.

text.p: French households were more optimistic in February, especially about the outlook for unemployment, official figures released on Tuesday showed.

The result is likely to be welcome news to France's conservative government, beset by record unemployment and growing public outcry over its apparent inability to make a dent in joblessness, which affects one of every eight adults.
National statistics institute INSEE reported that its consumer sentiment index rose to minus 29 last month from minus 30 in January. In December, the index was at minus 33.
The biggest improvement in the index was in unemployment, with the percentage of those expecting a rise in the jobless rate falling sharply.
The index on the outlook for unemployment fell to 49 in February from January's 61.
Those surveyed were asked if they thought unemployment would rise or fall in the coming months.
INSEE noted that the figure was in line with an improving trend established last autumn and interrupted in January.
The overall confidence level is an averarge of responses to questions about past and future living standads, past and future personal finances and whether it is currently a good time to spend.
